hooks.command: if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 3 'https://prymer.app/mcp/prymer' >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' 'Prymer is NOT reachable at https://prymer.app/mcp/prymer — the connection failed, so the Prymer MCP tools are unavailable this session. This is usually a local network problem, not a Prymer outage: corporate firewalls and DNS filters routinely block newly registered domains. Check whether that URL opens in a browser here, then try a different network (a phone hotspot is enough) to confirm. If it is filtered, ask your network administrator to allow the domain. Do not report a Prymer outage without first confirming it is unreachable from another network too.'; else printf '%s' 'Prymer is connected. Before starting work, call the get_context_for_injection MCP tool for the active Prymer channel (confirm it with the user; do not pick one from list_channels yourself) to load what other sessions already know.'; fi

printf '%s' 'If you finished a meaningful chunk of work, checkpoint it to the Prymer channel per its capture mode. Follow the guidance returned by get_context_for_injection: Auto means call share_session with trigger=agent_auto; Propose means ask the user first; Off means keep it private.'
